WikvenMainPage.description: Title of the page used as the wiki's main page, i.e. the static site root (written as <value>.html). Must be an imported page.

WikvenSettingsPage.description: Title of an auto-generated page holding the reader's display choices (colour theme, and the skin to read the site in), which a static export keeps in the browser. Stands in for Special:MobileOptions, which no bake writes. Empty disables it; a same-named source page takes precedence.

WikvenLicensesPage.description: Title of the page saying what the site publishes that is not its own, and under which licenses, linked from the footer of every page. A built site carries MediaWiki's own JavaScript and each skin's and extension's CSS, so something has to say so, and a page nobody links does not. The build writes what it ran on (MediaWiki, PHP and the database), then the extensions and skins with the version and license each declares for itself. Only MediaWiki's license is named among the first three: its scripts go out with the site and the other two do not, so a license beside them would read as a claim the site ships them. A source page of that name is used as written instead. Empty writes no page and drops the footer link, for a site that will acknowledge this its own way. A skin preview writes the page but does not link it, and says so.

WikvenSourceDirectory.description: Absolute path to the directory the build reads pages and images from. Set by WikvenSettings.php from WIKVEN_WORKDIR; empty means no source directory, which is what a wiki running the extension outside a build has.

WikvenSourceHistoryFile.description: Absolute path to a dump of the source tree's `git log`, used to date each page at the commit that last changed it and to name that commit's author. Set by WikvenSettings.php from WIKVEN_WORKDIR when actions/bake has mounted one; empty means the build reads git itself, if the source directory sits in a checkout it can reach, and dates every page at the commit being built if it cannot.

WikvenHtmlDirectory.description: Absolute path to the directory the build writes the static site to. Set by WikvenSettings.php from WIKVEN_WORKDIR (per-skin passes point it at a subdirectory); empty means nothing is written, which is what a wiki running the extension outside a build has.

WikvenAssetDirectory.description: Directory the build writes everything it generates into, under the output directory: the stylesheets, the script bundles, and the images and webfont files their CSS names. Left at the output root with ".", where they sit among the pages. One directory rather than one per kind because a stylesheet reaches its images by a path relative to itself, so they cannot be parted.

WikvenFooterUrl.description: Url that is added as a footer item.

WikvenEditUrl.description: URL template for the per-page "Edit" link. $1 is replaced with the page's percent-encoded source file name (e.g. "Getting Started.wikitext", "MediaWiki:Common.css"). Empty disables the link.

WikvenHistoryUrl.description: URL template for the per-page "View history" link. $1 is replaced with the page's percent-encoded source file name, as for WikvenEditUrl. Empty disables the link.

WikvenSiteUrl.description: Absolute URL the built site will be published at, including any path it is served under and ending in a slash -- "https://example.org/wiki/". Empty, the default, means the site has not said, and the features that need an absolute URL are then not written at all: a sitemap naming pages a crawler cannot resolve is worse than no sitemap. Nothing about the pages changes either way -- their links stay relative, so an export still works from any directory -- and only what is written about the site does. The build cannot work this out for itself: it installs against http://localhost:4000 and rewrites every page link to a file beside the one asking. Its scheme and host also fill $wgCanonicalServer, so what core and any extension build from that is right about the host. A value that is not an http or https URL is reported and read as empty.

WikvenViewSourceUrl.description: URL template for the per-page "View source" tab, linking to the page's source file in the repository. $1 is replaced with the page's percent-encoded source file name, as for WikvenEditUrl. Empty disables the tab.

WikvenLogos.description: Header logos, mirroring $wgLogos but keyed to image file names in the source directory. Each named file is uploaded like any other source image and the export copies it into the asset directory, so it is not embedded into every page.

WikvenRepositories.description: Sources for third-party extensions and skins listed in extensions/skins. A map of component name to a tarball/repository/package source, fetched by maintenance/fetchExtensions.php before MediaWiki loads them.

WikvenBundleWebfonts.description: When true and UniversalLanguageSelector is installed, bake its webfonts for the export's languages into a static stylesheet, so readers of a script their system lacks a font for see the intended typeface instead of tofu. Off by default because it adds font payload to the output.

WikvenFileNames.description: How a page is named in the output, and so what every link to it says. "readable", the default, names each page as its title is written: "Vector_(skin).html", "File:Bakery_oven.jpg.html". Those are the plainest URLs, and what a link carries is that name URL-encoded, so a static server asking for it finds it. Windows cannot hold a file whose name has a colon in it, so a site whose output directory is a Windows filesystem -- a bind mount from Docker Desktop, say -- cannot write a page outside the main namespace this way, and wants "encoded" instead: that leaves every escape the file cache made in place ("File%3ABakery_oven.jpg.html"), which any filesystem can hold, at the cost of URLs carrying that percent sign doubled. Four characters a Windows path cannot hold either -- a quote, an asterisk, a question mark and a backslash -- stay escaped under both, since they are rare in a title and keeping them costs nothing legible. An unrecognised value is reported and read as "readable".

WikvenBuildFor.description: Who the build is for. "site", the default, publishes: the chrome is trimmed to what a static host can stand behind, so the personal menu, toolbox, talk and watch affordances and section edit links are emptied, the article tabs become links to your source files, and a repository link goes in the footer. "skin-preview" is for a skin author baking a few pages to look at their skin, where every one of those edits is an edit to the thing being looked at: the chrome is left as the skin drew it, and no skin list or repository link is added. The skin-preview mode is experimental and stays so: a skin is written against several MediaWiki releases and a bake renders on the one this build carries, so it shows that skin on that version and evidences nothing about the others. Everything that makes the output work as files is the same either way -- links are still rewritten to ./X.html, styles and scripts are still baked to local copies. An unrecognised value is reported and read as "site".
